entries.name: CLOVER_MERCHANT_ID
entries.description: The Clover merchant's 13-character ID. Not a secret, but it names the client's business. The connector checks that the token answers for this merchant before it reads anything.
howToGet: In the merchant's Clover dashboard, open Settings > View all settings, then Merchants under About Your Business, and copy the 13-character merchant ID.
It also appears in the dashboard's address, after /merchants/.

entries.name: CLOVER_REGION
entries.description: Which Clover API host the merchant is on: north_america (api.clover.com), europe (api.eu.clover.com), latin_america (api.la.clover.com) or sandbox (apisandbox.dev.clover.com). The connector calls no other host.
howToGet: Use the region the merchant's Clover account was opened in: North America (the US and Canada), Europe or Latin America.
Use sandbox only for a developer test merchant.

entries.name: CLOVER_APP_ID
entries.description: App ID of the KaratOS app in the Clover Developer Dashboard, which is the OAuth client_id for refreshing tokens. With CLOVER_APP_SECRET and CLOVER_REFRESH_TOKEN, the connector keeps its own expiring tokens current.
howToGet: In the Clover Developer Dashboard, open Your Apps, pick the app, then App Settings, and copy the App ID.

In Requested Permissions, tick only Read merchant, Read orders, Read payments, Read inventory and Read customers. No Write permissions: Clover offers no way to check them later, so this is where read-only starts.

entries.name: CLOVER_APP_SECRET
entries.description: App secret of the Clover app. The connector doesn't send it; it is the key the instance seals its stored refresh token with, so rotating it means reconnecting the merchant.
howToGet: On the app's App Settings page in the Clover Developer Dashboard, copy the App Secret straight into the host's secret store.
After rotating it, reconnect the merchant and set a new CLOVER_REFRESH_TOKEN, because the stored token can no longer be decrypted.

entries.name: CLOVER_REFRESH_TOKEN
entries.description: The refresh token from connecting the merchant with Clover's v2 OAuth flow. Clover retires it on every refresh, so after the first sync the instance keeps the newest one encrypted in its database and this value only seeds it. Replacing it here (after reconnecting) takes over from the stored one.
howToGet: Have the merchant install the KaratOS app, then exchange the authorization code at /oauth/v2/token on the merchant's regional host.
Copy the refresh_token straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: CLOVER_API_TOKEN
entries.description: A merchant-specific API token, instead of the app sign-in, for one merchant (Clover documents these for test merchants). It doesn't expire; the connector only ever sends it with GET requests.
howToGet: In the merchant's Clover dashboard, open Settings > View all settings > API tokens and create a token.
Tick only the Read permissions for merchant, orders, payments, inventory and customers.
Copy it straight into the host's secret store.

entries.name: CLOVER_WEBHOOK_AUTH_CODE
entries.description: The Clover app's webhook auth code, which Clover sends in X-Clover-Auth with every notification. Only needed once webhooks are turned on; the scheduled sync works without it.
howToGet: In the Clover Developer Dashboard, open the app's App Settings > Webhooks, enter the webhook URL and verify it with the code Clover posts to it.
Copy the Clover Auth Code shown there straight into the host's secret store.
